To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the BS amplitude for a meson can be defined in a gauge-invariant fashion, and the gauge-invariant amplitude is broadened by fat links, which is consistent with the Lorentz-contraction of the wave function at nonzero momenta.
we have demonstrated that the gauge invariant Bethe-Salpe ter amplitude can be used to extract information about the Lorentz structure of the meson wave function.

we have demonstrated a qualitative demonstration of the broadening of the gauge-invariant Bethe-Salpe ter amplitude for the pion at nonzero momentum, and have extracted the relative admixture between l = 0 states and l = 1 states for ρ mesons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the qq Betbe-Salpeter amplitude for mesons, and the study of the resulting wave functions.
the calculation of the Bethe-Salpetr (BS) amplitudes of mesons and their density correlation functions in lattice QCD.
the study of the Bethe-Salpetr amplitudes and their gauge dependence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Bethe-Salpe-ter amplitude for the pion is a very useful quantity, which can be calculated with high precision and can be used to obtain information about the wave function of the pion.
the gauge invariant BS amplitudes are not only gauge independent, but also more stable under the use of fat gauge links.
all the observables studied here are consistent with a simple hydrogenlike wave function for the pion and ρ mesons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gauge-invariant BS amplitudes are useful for studying meson structure and that the use of fat links is essential for a quantitative analysis.
the use of fat links in gauge-invariant definitions for the Bethe-Salpetr amplitudes is essential to obtain the proper Lorentz contraction at nonzero momentum.
we find that the Bethe-Salpetr amplitudes are sensitive to the choice of gauge fixing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gauge-invariant definitions are not a good starting point for the calculation of meson wave functions, as their use leads to a broadening of the wave function that is not physical.
, in the continuum limit, the gauge-invariant definition of the Bethe-Salpter amplitude is a useful tool for extracting the wave function of mesons.
the gauge-invariance of the BS amplitudes can be achieved at finite lattice spacing, and that these observables provide a good description of the wave functions of the hadrons.
